entries.title: Nonnegative grand-canonical DLR specification
entries.statement: For a locally finite exterior eta, finite z>0 and beta>0, and measurable nonnegative pair potential v, the conditional law in bounded B assigns the n-particle sector unnormalized density z^n/n! times exp(-beta H_B), where H_B is the sum of internal pair interactions and interactions with eta. The empty configuration has weight one. There is no neutralizing background or fixed particle-count constraint; the partition sum includes n=0.
assumptions: Ordinary grand-canonical DLR law on locally finite configurations
Nonnegative pair interaction, zero empty energy
No neutralizing background, negative external energy, or fixed local count

entries.title: Uniform DLR void bound and arbitrarily large holes
entries.statement: For a probability law on locally finite configurations in R^3 satisfying the ordinary grand-canonical DLR specification with finite activity z>0, finite inverse temperature beta>0, measurable nonnegative pair interaction, zero empty energy, no background, no negative one-body energy, and no fixed local count, each bounded B has 1<=Xi_B<=exp(z|B|), so its conditional void probability is at least exp(-z|B|) almost surely. For m disjoint equal-volume regions of volume V, the probability all are occupied is at most (1-exp(-zV))^m, by exterior conditioning and induction, without independence. Almost surely there are arbitrarily large empty balls, and no bijection from any full-rank lattice, even one selected from the configuration, can have globally bounded displacement. This applies to ordinary three-dimensional Riesz DLR laws with s>3; it does not rule out lattice-periodic probability laws or address renormalized s<=3 specifications. The universal finite bound is sharp for the zero-potential Poisson specification. Independently checked by w536; no novelty claim is made.
entries.proof_text: The local energy H_B is the nonnegative sum of internal and exterior pair terms; the chemical-potential contribution is already encoded in z^n. The empty term of Xi_B is one. Nonnegative energy bounds each Boltzmann factor by one, so Xi_B<=sum_n (z|B|)^n/n!=exp(z|B|), giving the conditional empty probability 1/Xi_B>=p=exp(-z|B|). For disjoint B_i of volume V, the events that the other regions are occupied are exterior-measurable for B_i. Conditioning on the exterior of the last region bounds the probability that all m are occupied by (1-p) times the probability for the first m-1; induction gives (1-p)^m. For each integer radius choose a deterministic infinite sequence of disjoint balls. Every tail has probability zero of being wholly occupied, by the finite bound as m tends to infinity. A countable union over tails and intersection over integer radii gives infinitely many empty balls of every integer radius almost surely. A full-rank lattice has finite covering radius c. If a bijection displaced its sites by at most M, every ball of radius R>c+M would contain a particle. On the same probability-one event, choose an integer R>c+M; the empty-ball property contradicts this. This is pathwise and permits a configuration-dependent lattice without an uncountable probability intersection. For v=0, the specification is Poisson of intensity z, and disjoint void events give equality in the universal bound. At fixed z with empty exterior the finite-volume Riesz partition sum tends to the same value as beta tends to zero, by termwise dominated convergence and domination by the exponential series.
assumptions: Ordinary grand-canonical DLR law on locally finite configurations
Nonnegative pair interaction, zero empty energy
No neutralizing background, negative external energy, or fixed local count

entries.title: Refuted global lattice-displacement bridge for ordinary DLR gases
entries.statement: Refuted auxiliary bridge, not a statement of P0309: a finite-temperature ordinary grand-canonical Gibbs law with finite activity and measurable nonnegative pair interaction is supported on configurations admitting a globally bounded displacement bijection from a full-rank lattice. Under the explicitly stated ordinary-DLR assumptions this assertion contradicts the uniform conditional void bound and arbitrarily large holes. It is stronger than lattice periodicity of a probability law, which is not refuted. A fixed-count or renormalized long-range specification is outside this obstruction. Independent referee w536 checked the counterargument.
assumptions: Ordinary grand-canonical DLR law on locally finite configurations
Nonnegative pair interaction, zero empty energy
No neutralizing background, negative external energy, or fixed local count

relations.rationale: The conditional void estimate uses the n=0 weight and nonnegative interaction of this exact specification.
The auxiliary bridge is explicitly restricted to the same ordinary grand-canonical specification.
Independently checked refutation: arbitrarily large holes contradict finite lattice covering radius plus globally bounded displacement. This auxiliary bridge is not the original P0309 target.
Both address a limitation of using local harmonic localization to conclude a full Gibbs crystal: the prior card explicitly leaves defect and competing-configuration control open.
P0309 seeks low-positive-temperature Riesz crystalline Gibbs phases; this draft constrains one stronger configuration-support criterion in its ordinary s>3 regime.
